comparable_cases.why_comparable: This is an agency referral for the exact same address (200 Capp St) in 2019, approving continuation of the existing bar use (DBA Uptown) with a Type 48 license in the NCT-MISSION district and Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Planning approved continuation of the bar use at this location but explicitly stated no intensification or expansion would be allowed in the Mission Alcoholic Beverage SUD without a conditional use authorization. This is an agency referral, not a Commission hearing, so it shows administrative approval but not full discretionary review.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Earlier agency referral at the same address (200 Capp St) in 2015 approving an ownership transfer of the Type 48 license for the existing bar use (DBA Uptown) per Planning Code Section 249.60(c) governing the Mission Alcoholic Beverage SUD.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Planning approved a Type 48 ownership transfer at this exact location under the Mission Alcoholic Beverage SUD rules. Both this and the 2019 referral were continuations of an existing bar, not establishment of a new bar use, which is the critical distinction in the Special Use District.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Agency referral 195 meters away at 2901 16th St approving a Type 48 license for a restaurant/bar use. The record explicitly states the license was transferred from within the Mission Alcohol Restrict SUD (from 2950 16th Street City Club), demonstrating compliance with the district's transfer requirement.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Planning approved a Type 48 bar use in the Mission Alcoholic Beverage SUD by confirming the license was transferred from another location already within the district, as required by Planning Code Section 249.60(c). This shows the pathway for establishing bar use in the SUD: transfer from within the district.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Second agency referral for the same 2901 16th St project (Board of Supervisors/Public Convenience or Necessity referral), 195 meters away, also noting the Type 48 license transfer from within the Mission Alcohol Restrict SUD and that it was not treated as a change of use under Planning Code Section 843.45.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: The dual referrals show both Planning and ABC coordination was required. The finding that restaurant-to-bar was not a 'change of use' under Section 843.45 when the license came from within the district suggests flexibility when the SUD transfer requirement is met.

Validity: The authorization and right vested by virtue of this action is valid for three (3) years from the effective date of the Motion. The Department of Building Inspection shall have issued a Building Permit or Site Permit to construct the project and/or commence the approved use within this three-year period. (standard)

Expiration and Renewal: Should a Building or Site Permit be sought after the three (3) year period has lapsed, the project sponsor must seek a renewal of this Authorization by filing an application for an amendment to the original Authorization or a new application for Authorization. Should the project sponsor decline to so file, and decline to withdraw the permit application, the Commission shall conduct a public hearing in order to consider the revocation of the Authorization. (standard)

Diligent Pursuit: Once a site or Building Permit has been issued, construction must commence within the timeframe required by the Department of Building Inspection and be continued diligently to completion. Failure to do so shall be grounds for the Commission to consider revoking the approval if more than three (3) years have passed since this Authorization was approved. (standard)

Extension: All time limits in the preceding three paragraphs may be extended at the discretion of the Zoning Administrator where implementation of the project is delayed by a public agency, an appeal or a legal challenge and only by the length of time for which such public agency, appeal or challenge has caused delay . (standard)

Conformity with Current Law: No application for Building Permit, Site Permit, or other entitlement shall be approved unless it complies with all applicable provisions of City Codes in effect at the time of such approval. (standard)

Space for the collection and storage of recyclable and compostable materials that meets the size, location, accessibility and other standards specified by the San Francisco Recycling Program shall be provided at the ground level of the buildings. Noise: Plans submitted with the building permit application for the approved project shall incorporate acoustical insulation and other sound proofing measures to control noise. (standard)

filing_playbook.action: Request a written answer from San Francisco Planning confirming the current count of eating and drinking uses in NCT-MISSION against the 179-unit cap.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Submit a Letter of Determination request or call the zoning information desk at Planning and ask for the count of Restaurants, Limited Restaurants, and Bars in the Mission Street NCT district as of today, against the 179-unit cap in Planning Code Section 754 Table 754 Note 7, in effect from January 14, 2024. Ask whether a new bar at 200 Capp St would exceed the cap. If the cap is already reached, ask whether the prior bar use at the address (DBA Uptown, operated until February 21, 2024) counts toward the cap and whether reopening the bar use would be treated as a new use or a continuation.

filing_playbook.action: After the Planning Commission approves the CUA, file the Type 48 license transfer application with ABC, and submit the CUA approval as part of the ABC application.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: ABC will refer the application to Planning and to the Police Department ABC Liaison Unit. Planning will issue a referral response confirming the CUA has been granted. The Police Department will review the operator's background and the location. Budget 90 to 180 days from filing to ABC issuing the transferred license, plus time for public posting and any protests. Do not open or serve alcohol until ABC issues the license.

filing_playbook.action: After the building permit is issued and construction is complete, schedule the final DBI inspection and apply for the health permit to operate from San Francisco Department of Public Health.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: The health permit application will be referred to Planning, which will confirm the CUA and building permit are in place. DPH will inspect to confirm the bar meets health code requirements for a beverage service facility: handwashing sinks, janitorial facilities, and proper storage. The permit is issued after the inspection passes. All staff who handle drinks or ice must obtain California Food Handler Cards within 30 days of hire, and at least one owner or manager must hold a Certified Food Protection Manager certificate if any food is served.

timeline_cost.notes: The day and cost ranges cover the Conditional Use Authorization (120 to 300 days, $3,100 to $15,000 per the catalog) from filing to Commission approval, which is the critical path. These are times and costs to approval for the CUA. ABC license transfer (90 to 180 days, cost depends on the purchase price of the license from the seller, typically $100,000 to $450,000 in San Francisco) and the building permit (14 to 120 days, $800 to $15,000) run in parallel or follow the CUA. The CUA timeline depends on pre-application meetings, environmental review, hearing scheduling, and any appeals; the catalog estimates 120 to 300 days. The building permit depends on the scope of tenant improvements and plan completeness. Government fees for the CUA, building permit, business registration, sign permit, and health permit total roughly $4,000 to $17,000; the Type 48 license purchase from another bar is the largest cost but is paid to a private seller, not a government agency, so it is not included in the cost range shown here. If the count of eating and drinking uses in NCT-MISSION is already at or above the 179-unit cap, the CUA may not be grantable, in which case no time or cost to approval can be given until Planning confirms the count.

records_summary: 200 Capp St operated as a bar (DBA Uptown) with a Type 48 full-bar license until February 21, 2024, when the license was surrendered—the same day as this report. The space sits in the Mission Street NCT district where a bar is a conditional use, and inside the Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District, which requires any new bar to use a Type 48 license transferred from another bar already located within the district. The block is densely developed with food and drink businesses: 21 registered businesses within 500 feet and four active ABC on-sale licenses. The records contain no dated Planning Commission decisions for comparable bar or nightlife uses within 1,000 feet in the last ten years, so no approval rate can be shown.
